questions.prompt: What does junto seat read let one seat do to another?

choices.why: seat read carries no input authority.

choices.text: Read its state and screen, nothing more
choices.why: seat read is read-only: no input, resize or signal.
seat read carries no resize authority.
No seat command stops another seat.

questions.prompt: How does msg send --prompt differ from plain mail?

choices.why: A prompt needs the same line as any mail.

choices.text: It types the full text at once, as its own turn
choices.why: A prompt is typed whole, as a turn of its own, without waiting for the batch plain mail gathers in (2 s quiet, 10 s at most); plain mail is typed up to 2,500 characters.

choices.text: It is typed even while the operator is typing in the box
choices.why: A prompt waits for a free input box like any mail; Junto never types over a draft.

questions.prompt: Mail for a seat arrives one second after other mail for it. What happens?

choices.text: Each is typed as its own turn
choices.why: Mail within two seconds of other mail is typed together.

choices.text: They are typed together as one turn
choices.why: Mail within 2 seconds of other mail is batched, typed at most 10 seconds after the first.

choices.text: The second waits for the next session
choices.why: Batching happens within the running session.
Mail is never dropped; it waits with no time limit when it cannot be typed.
